newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian shares notch up gains in good trade.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian shares notch up gains in good trade.

text.p: Egyptian share prices gained slightly on Thursday in trade powered by realty firm Medinet Nasr Housing and Development.
The Capital Market Authority index added 1.41 points to end at 336.56 in 52.1 million pounds ($15.3 million) worth of trade.
"I believe the market will keep climbing from here," said Omar Ramzi, general manager at Delta EAB.
Merrill Lynch said in an analysis that in its view the Cairo stock exchange was one of the region's most attractively valued and it expected an upturn despite recent lows.

"The prolonged market weakness, with falling prices and weak trading volumes, has reflected both problems with settlement, which have delayed the flow of foreign money into the bourse, and also the withdrawal of retail investors who had entered the market towards the end of the bull run."
"However, we believe that there is now the potential for considerable upside in the market," the report said.
Medinet Nasr rose 0.02 pounds in 7.2 million pounds worth of turnover to close at 237.92.
Ramzi attributed the high turnover to investors obtaining their coupons after a share split about a month ago.
The blue-chip Commercial International Bank, was active with 2.3 million pounds of trade. Its share slid 0.13 pounds to 73.52.

Suez Cement, which announced on Thursday that its first half profits rose, closed 0.35 pounds higher at 63.51 when more than 27,000 shares changed hands for turnover worth 1.7 million pounds. It was the most active cement share.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 454.02 points from 451.91 points on Wednesday and that for the rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 250.78 from 249.78.
Of the 98 shares traded, 53 rose, 28 ended lower and 17 remained unchanged.
